title: Biff a la Lindstrom (Swedish beef and beetroot patties)

ingredients.name: mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam to serve

steps: Combine the beef, egg, onion, grated potato, beetroot, capers, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Mix gently but thoroughly with your hands until the mixture binds, then chill for 15 minutes.
Shape into 8 flat, round patties with wet hands.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until browned and cooked through.
Serve with mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam or a fried egg on top.

title: Blabarssoppa (Swedish bilberry soup)

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen bilberries or blueberries
whipped cream, vanilla ice cream or milk to serve

steps: Put the berries, water and sugar into a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer for about 10 minutes.
Mash or blend a part of the berries to make the soup smoother, if you like.
Dissolve the potato starch in the cold water, then stir it into the soup.
Simmer for another minute or two, stirring, until lightly thickened.
Taste and add sugar if needed.
Serve warm or chilled, topped with cream or ice cream or with milk poured over.

title: Flaskpannkaka (Swedish oven pancake with bacon)

ingredients.name: thick-cut bacon or salt pork, cut into small strips

steps: Heat the oven to 225 C (435 F).
Fry the bacon strips in an ovenproof frying pan or roasting tin until they are cooked and have rendered fat, but are not yet crisp.
Whisk the flour with the salt and half of the milk until smooth, then whisk in the eggs and the rest of the milk to a thin batter.
Pour the batter over the bacon in the hot pan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed up and golden brown at the edges and set in the middle.
Cut into squares and serve warm with lingonberry jam.

title: Flygande Jacob (Flying Jacob, Swedish chicken, bacon and banana casserole)

ingredients.name: chilli sauce or ketchup mixed with a pinch of chilli
cooked rice and a green salad to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F).
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and drain it on paper towels.
Whip the cream until it just holds soft peaks and fold in the chilli sauce.
Spread the chicken in a baking dish and scatter the bacon and banana slices over it.
Spoon the cream mixture over the top and bake for about 20 minutes until bubbling and lightly golden.
Sprinkle the peanuts over and serve with rice and a green salad.

title: Hasselbackspotatis (Hasselback potatoes, fan-sliced roast potatoes)

ingredients.name: grated hard cheese or chopped herbs to finish (optional)

steps: Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F).
Lay each potato between the handles of two wooden spoons, or chopsticks, so that the blade cannot cut all the way through.
Cut thin slices of about 3 mm across each potato, stopping at the spoons so the slices stay joined at the base.
Rinse the potatoes briefly, pat them dry and place them in a baking dish.
Brush them with the melted butter and oil and sprinkle with salt.
Roast for 30 minutes, then brush again with the fat, sprinkle on the breadcrumbs and roast for another 20 to 25 minutes until crisp and golden at the edges.
Finish with cheese or herbs if using, and serve hot.

title: Janssons frestelse (Jansson's temptation, potato and sprat gratin)

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
sprats or anchovy fillets in spiced brine (Swedish ansjovis), brine reserved

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F) and butter a medium baking dish.
Melt half of the butter in a pan and cook the sliced onions gently for about 10 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Layer half of the potatoes in the dish, then the onions and the fish fillets, and finish with the remaining potatoes.
Mix the cream with 2 tablespoons of the reserved fish brine and a little pepper and pour half of it over the potatoes.
Sprinkle with the breadcrumbs and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake for 20 minutes, then pour over the rest of the cream and bake for another 25 to 30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot as part of a smorgasbord or with a green salad.

title: Kladdkaka (Swedish sticky chocolate cake)

ingredients.name: whipped cream or ice cream and berries to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 175 C (350 F) and grease a 20 cm springform tin; dust the greased tin with breadcrumbs or cocoa.
Whisk the eggs and sugar together briefly, just until combined; do not whip until fluffy.
Add the melted butter, flour, cocoa, vanilla and salt and stir until smooth.
Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 15 to 20 minutes; the surface should be set while the middle is still soft and sticky.
Leave to cool in the tin for at least 15 minutes before releasing it.
Serve with whipped cream, ice cream or berries.

title: Knack (Swedish Christmas toffee)

ingredients.name: golden syrup or light corn syrup

steps: Place the cream, sugar and syrup in a heavy-based pan with high sides, as the mixture bubbles up.

Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then cook without stirring too much until a spoonful dropped into a glass of cold water forms a firm ball, about 125 C (257 F) on a thermometer.
Remove from the heat, stir in the butter and the almonds if using.
Pour or ladle the toffee into paper cases and let it set for several hours at room temperature.
Take great care at every stage, as hot sugar causes serious burns.
Store in an airtight container, between sheets of baking paper.

title: Korv stroganoff (Swedish sausage stroganoff with rice)

ingredients.name: falukorv, or other mild smoked cooking sausage, cut into strips

steps: Melt the butter in a large pan and fry the sausage strips over medium-high heat until lightly browned.
Add the onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, ketchup and paprika and cook for a minute.
Pour in the stock and cream and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens a little.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over the cooked rice.

title: Kottsoppa (Swedish beef and root vegetable soup)

ingredients.name: beef chuck or brisket, in a piece
chopped parsley and mustard to serve

steps: Put the beef in a large pot with the water, onion, allspice, bay leaves and salt and bring slowly to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Lift out the beef, strain the broth if you want it clear and return it to the pot.
Add the carrots, leek, swede and potatoes and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Cut the beef into bite-sized pieces and return it to the soup.
Taste for salt and serve hot, sprinkled with parsley, with mustard on the side.

title: Lingonberry jam (Swedish lingonsylt for meatballs and pancakes)

ingredients.name: lingonberries (fresh or frozen; cranberries may be used instead)

steps: Rinse the berries and discard any soft ones or stalks.
Put the berries, sugar and water in a wide saucepan and bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, skimming off any foam, until the berries have burst and the jam is lightly thickened.
Let it cool slightly, then spoon into clean, sterilised jars.
Keep it refrigerated and use within 2 to 3 weeks, or freeze for longer storage.
Serve with meatballs, potato pancakes, pancakes or porridge.

title: Nyponsoppa (Swedish rose hip soup)

ingredients.name: whipped cream, vanilla ice cream or almond biscuits to serve

steps: Rinse the rose hips and soak them in the water for a few hours or overnight.
Simmer the rose hips in the same water for about 30 minutes until very soft.
Blend or mash them and press everything through a fine sieve to remove the seeds and hairs.
Return the strained liquid to the pan and add the sugar.
Dissolve the potato starch in the cold water and stir it into the pan; bring to a simmer, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Serve warm or chilled with whipped cream, a scoop of vanilla ice cream or almond biscuits.

title: Prinsesstarta (Swedish princess cake with green marzipan)

ingredients.name: icing sugar and a pink marzipan rose to decorate

steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale and thick, about 5 minutes, then fold in the flour and baking powder.
Bake in a lined 22 cm springform tin at 175 C (350 F) for 25 to 30 minutes; cool, then slice into three layers.

For the pastry cream, whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour with a little milk, heat the rest of the milk with the vanilla, whisk into the yolk mixture and return to the pan; cook, stirring, until thick, then cool with film touching the surface.
Spread the bottom layer with jam and a layer of pastry cream.
Add the middle layer, then spread with whipped cream, and top with the last layer.
Pile the rest of the whipped cream on top in a high dome, smoothing it to cover the sides.
Roll out the marzipan thinly, drape it over the cake and trim the edges around the base.
Dust with icing sugar and decorate with a marzipan rose; chill for several hours before serving.

title: Pytt i panna (Swedish potato, meat and onion hash with fried egg)

ingredients.name: firm potatoes, cut into small cubes
leftover cooked meat or sausage, diced (beef, ham, pork or falukorv)
pickled beetroot slices and Worcestershire sauce to serve

steps: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 5 to 6 minutes until barely tender, then drain well and dry them in the colander.
Heat half of the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the potatoes until golden and crisp on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add more fat to the pan and fry the onion for 3 minutes, then add the meat and fry until browned.
Return the potatoes to the pan, season and toss everything together for 2 to 3 minutes.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan in the remaining butter, sunny side up.
Divide the hash between plates, top each with a fried egg and serve with pickled beetroot and a few drops of Worcestershire sauce.

title: Semla (Swedish cardamom bun with almond paste and cream)

ingredients.name: almond paste (marzipan with a high almond content)

steps: Mix the yeast with the warm milk, then combine it with the flour, sugar, cardamom, salt, butter and egg and knead for 10 minutes to a soft dough; rise for an hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls, place them on a lined tray, cover and prove for 30 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 225 C (435 F) for 10 to 12 minutes until golden, then cool on a rack.
Slice off the top of each bun as a lid and scoop out some of the crumb from the inside.
Mash the scooped crumb with the almond paste and the milk to a thick smooth paste.
Spoon the almond paste into each bun, pipe or spoon a big swirl of whipped cream on top and set the lid on.
Dust with icing sugar and eat straight away, traditionally on Shrove Tuesday.

title: Toast Skagen (Swedish prawn salad on toast)

ingredients.name: cooked peeled small prawns, patted dry
finely chopped fresh dill, plus sprigs to garnish
salt and white pepper to taste

steps: Mix the mayonnaise, creme fraiche, dill, lemon juice and mustard, if using, in a bowl.
Gently fold in the prawns and season with salt and pepper; chill for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter in a frying pan and fry the bread slices until golden on both sides, or toast them and butter them.
Trim the crusts if you like and cut each slice in half.
Spoon the prawn salad generously onto each toast.
Top with roe, dill sprigs and a lemon wedge on the side and serve straight away.

title: Tunnbrod (Swedish soft thin flatbread)
steps: Stir the yeast into the warm water or milk and mix with the oil, syrup, rye flour and about half of the plain flour.
Add the salt and enough plain flour to make a soft dough; knead for 8 to 10 minutes and let it rise for an hour.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and let them rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Roll each piece out very thin into rounds about 25 cm wide, pricking them all over with a fork.
Cook them one at a time in a hot, dry frying pan or on a griddle for about 1 minute on each side until spotted brown and cooked through.
Stack the breads under a clean cloth to keep them soft and serve with butter, cheese or cold cuts, or use as wraps.

title: Wallenbergare (Swedish veal patties with cream)

ingredients.name: minced veal (or minced chicken or pork as a substitute)
mashed potatoes, peas and lingonberry jam to serve

steps: Chill the veal and the bowl thoroughly; the mixture works best when cold.
Work the veal with the salt and pepper in a food processor, or beat by hand, until sticky.
Add the egg yolks one at a time, then pour in the cold cream gradually and mix just until smooth and creamy.
With wet hands shape into 4 thick patties and coat all sides gently in the breadcrumbs, pressing so they stick.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat until foaming.
Fry the patties for 5 to 6 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through, handling them carefully as they are soft.
Serve with mashed potatoes, peas, browned butter and lingonberry jam.
